Let  

* \(T\) = capacity of the fuel tank (in gallons)  
* After the last fill the car was driven \(488\) miles.  
* When it is stopped now, adding \(4\) gallons will bring the tank back to full.

---

### 1.  Relate the fuel used to the tank capacity  

If after the \(488\) miles the driver needs only \(4\) gallons to fill the tank, then the amount of fuel that has been **consumed** is  

\[
\text{fuel used}=T-4\quad\text{gallons}.
\]

---

### 2.  Compute the fuel consumption per mile  

\[
\text{fuel per mile}= \frac{T-4}{488}\quad\text{gallons/mile}.
\]

---

### 3.  Find how many miles a full tank can give  

The number of miles that can be travelled on a full tank (\(M\)) is  

\[
M = \frac{T}{\text{fuel per mile}}
    = \frac{T}{\dfrac{T-4}{488}}
    = \frac{488\,T}{T-4}.
\]

---

### 4.  Insert the given tank capacity  

The specification says the tank holds **310** (i.e. **31.0**) gallons.  
Thus \(T = 31\).

\[
M = \frac{488 \times 31}{31-4}
   = \frac{15128}{27}
   \approx 560.15\text{ miles}.
\]

Rounded to the nearest mile, Mmesoọma can travel **560 miles** on a full tank.
